title: The Financial Crisis: Risk and Balance Sheets
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: 四つの原文段落と全九つの学習対象を保持し、元の記述問題を英語四択へ変換しました。

passages.text:
The financial crisis that intensified in 2008 began neither on a single day nor with a single institution. Years of rising house prices encouraged lenders, borrowers, and investors to expect that refinancing or resale would cover weak repayment capacity. Mortgage standards deteriorated in parts of the market, while loans were pooled into securities and sold through a long chain of originators, arrangers, rating agencies, and investors.

Securitization can distribute risk when underlying loans are understood, incentives are aligned, and investors can bear losses. In this episode, however, complex structures made exposure difficult to trace. Highly rated tranches appeared safe even though their performance depended on correlated housing outcomes. When prices fell and defaults rose, diversification across many similar loans offered less protection than models had implied.

Losses became systemic because many institutions were highly leveraged and depended on short-term funding. A modest decline in asset values could therefore erase a thin layer of equity. Creditors who could not identify which firms were solvent demanded cash or refused to renew funding. Forced sales then pushed prices lower, weakening other balance sheets. This feedback loop resembles a run: individually defensive actions can collectively make the system less stable.

The bankruptcy of a major investment bank in September 2008 was a powerful accelerator, not the complete cause. Governments and central banks responded with liquidity support, guarantees, capital injections, and fiscal measures. These actions may limit collapse while raising difficult questions about moral hazard and distribution: whose losses are absorbed, whose contracts are protected, and what conditions accompany rescue? Crisis analysis is incomplete until it follows both the transmission of risk and the allocation of recovery costs.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: One bankruptcy created every vulnerability in 2008.

options.label: B
options.text: The crisis emerged when housing losses interacted with opaque securities, leverage, short-term funding, and policy choices.

options.label: C
options.text: Securitization always eliminates risk.

options.label: D
options.text: Only borrowers made decisions that mattered.

questions.answer: 正解：B。住宅損失が不透明な証券化、高レバレッジ、短期資金、政策対応と相互作用した危機です。Aは引き金を完全原因にし、Cは条件付き効果を絶対化し、Dは制度連鎖を消します。

questions.prompt: How did expectations of rising house prices conceal weak repayment capacity?

options.label: A
options.text: Borrowers and lenders expected refinancing or resale to cover debts, delaying visible evidence that current income was insufficient.

options.label: B
options.text: Higher prices immediately improved every borrower's wages.

options.label: C
options.text: Refinancing permanently removed all debt and default risk.

options.label: D
options.text: Market participants expected house prices to fall continuously.

questions.answer: 正解：A。借換えや売却で債務を処理できるとの期待が、現在所得による返済能力不足の顕在化を遅らせました。B～Dは所得、債務、価格期待について本文と異なります。

questions.prompt: The word “correlated” in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: likely to deteriorate together because of a shared factor

options.label: B
options.text: legally guaranteed by a central bank

options.label: C
options.text: randomly selected from unrelated countries

options.label: D
options.text: impossible to value under any condition

questions.answer: 正解：A。同じ住宅市場要因に依存して同方向に悪化しやすいことです。Bは保証、Cは相関の反対、Dは評価困難を「常に不可能」へ強めすぎます。

questions.prompt: Why can securitization either distribute risk or conceal it?

options.label: A
options.text: Transparent pools with aligned incentives can place losses with capable investors, but complex repackaging of similarly exposed loans can hide location and correlation of risk.

options.label: B
options.text: Pooling loans guarantees that their risks are unrelated.

options.label: C
options.text: Complexity always makes underlying loans easier to understand.

options.label: D
options.text: The incentives of loan originators and final investors never matter.

questions.answer: 正解：A。透明性と誘因整合があれば負担可能な投資家へ分散できますが、同じ要因に依存する融資の複雑な再包装は危険の所在と相関を隠します。B～Dは条件を無視します。

questions.prompt: Why can a small asset-price decline seriously damage a highly leveraged institution with a thin layer of equity?

options.label: A
options.text: Because equity is the residual after liabilities, a small percentage loss on large debt-financed assets can erase it and raise doubts about solvency.

options.label: B
options.text: Because falling asset values automatically increase equity.

options.label: C
options.text: Because leverage means the institution has no liabilities.

options.label: D
options.text: Because creditors ignore whether a firm can meet its obligations.

questions.answer: 正解：A。自己資本は資産から債務を引いた薄い残余なので、借入で膨らんだ資産の小幅下落でも全て失われ得ます。Bは会計関係と逆、C・Dはレバレッジと債権者行動を誤ります。

questions.prompt: Which option best describes the feedback loop in paragraph 3?

options.label: A
options.text: Every firm can sell safely because all firms act independently.

options.label: B
options.text: Defensive withdrawals and forced sales can lower prices and weaken other firms' balance sheets.

options.label: C
options.text: Falling prices automatically increase every firm's equity.

options.label: D
options.text: A guarantee removes all future incentives to take risk.

questions.answer: 正解：B。個別には防御的な資金引揚げと売却が価格を下げ、他社の財務を傷め、さらに売却を促します。Aは同時行動、Cは会計関係、Dはモラルハザードを誤ります。

questions.prompt: Why is the September 2008 investment-bank bankruptcy described as an accelerator rather than the complete cause?

options.label: A
options.text: Housing-price expectations, weak lending standards, opaque securities, leverage, and short-term funding dependence had already created vulnerability.

options.label: B
options.text: The bankruptcy occurred before any risky lending or securities existed.

options.label: C
options.text: The event had no effect on confidence or funding markets.

options.label: D
options.text: A single event cannot ever influence a financial crisis.

questions.answer: 正解：A。破綻前から住宅価格期待、審査悪化、複雑証券、高レバレッジ、短期資金依存が蓄積していました。Bは時系列、Cは加速効果、Dは本文より過度に一般化しています。

questions.prompt: What does the final sentence say a complete crisis analysis must examine?

options.label: A
options.text: Both how risk moved through loans, securities, institutions, and the economy, and how recovery costs were divided among groups

options.label: B
options.text: Only the date of the largest bankruptcy

options.label: C
options.text: Only whether central banks supplied liquidity

options.label: D
options.text: Risk transmission without considering who bore losses or rescue costs

questions.answer: 正解：A。融資から証券・金融機関・実体経済へのリスク伝播と、株主・債権者・納税者・失業者などへの回復費用配分の両方を追う必要があります。B～Dは片面だけです。

questions.prompt: Which rescue conditions best balance immediate stability with limiting future moral hazard?

options.label: A
options.text: Protect essential payments and credit, impose losses on existing shareholders first, restrict failed-risk bonuses, disclose exposures, charge for temporary guarantees, and require more capital and credible resolution plans.

options.label: B
options.text: Protect every investor fully and permanently without fees, disclosure, or reform.

options.label: C
options.text: Let executives retain all rewards while taxpayers absorb every loss.

options.label: D
options.text: Refuse all liquidity support even when payment and credit systems face collapse.

questions.answer: 正解：A。不可欠な機能を守りつつ、株主負担、報酬制限、開示、期限・料金、資本増強、破綻処理計画で将来の救済期待を抑えます。B・Cはモラルハザードを強め、Dは現在の崩壊抑制を放棄します。
